name: spin
algorithm: t workers (Mk: tasks; Go: goroutines; C, Rust and Zig: OS threads) each take the standard short-section lock n times and add one to a shared counter: Mk's atomic.Spin, C11's atomic_flag spin lock, and, where the std has no spin lock, its Mutex (Go, Rust, Zig). Prints the counter (t * n) (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the only arithmetic is the counter, which stays below 2^40

models.go: goroutines (GOMAXPROCS 8), sync.Mutex (no spin lock in std)
models.rust: OS threads, std::sync::Mutex (no spin lock in std)
models.zig: OS threads, std.Io.Mutex (no spin lock in std)

no_counts: B24 does not apply: the checksum, the count, shows that no increment was lost
notes: Concurrency row (B19): every column runs on logical CPUs 0, 2, ..., 14 (mask 0x5555, eight physical cores, one logical CPU each) with 8 threads (MK_CARRIERS=8, GOMAXPROCS=8). C, Rust and Zig use OS threads, labelled so.

Only C has a spin lock in its standard library; the Go, Rust and Zig cells are their std mutexes, which spin briefly before they park, so the row compares the best std facility for a short critical section, not one algorithm.
Written by std-missing (status/std-missing.md, M6 session 2); checksums from the workload's arithmetic, printed by the Mk build on the owner's machine, 2026-11-07.
